fields.name: n_subdivisions

fields.help: Fuselage body-of-revolution stations, incl. diameter (width) and length breakdown.
fields.label: Fuselage
fields.name: fuselage

fields.help: Ratio of wetted (exposed, both sides) surface area to planform area for a thin wing. Used by the drag buildup.
fields.label: Wing wetted-area factor
fields.name: wing_wetted_area_factor

fields.help: Correction factor on pi*diameter*length for a non-cylindrical (tapered nose/tail) fuselage body.
fields.label: Fuselage wetted-area factor
fields.name: fuselage_wetted_factor

fields.help: Margin applied to the static reaction load when selecting/verifying tire count -- real gear is sized so the rated tire load is never fully consumed by static load alone, leaving margin for dynamic (braking, turning, rough-field) loads. Raymer: ~1.07 typical for a preliminary sizing pass.
fields.label: Tire load safety factor
fields.name: tire_safety_factor

fields.help: Wheels on the nose gear strut. 0 = auto: 1 for light aircraft, 2 (the near-universal choice for CS-25/FAR-25 transports) once MTOW exceeds nlg_dual_wheel_mtow_kg.
fields.label: Nose-gear wheel count (0 = auto)
fields.name: n_nlg_wheels

fields.help: Auto-sizing switches from a single to a dual (twin) nose wheel above this MTOW -- below it, transport-category aircraft still commonly fly single nose wheels.
fields.label: MTOW threshold for dual nose wheels
fields.name: nlg_dual_wheel_mtow_kg

fields.help: Number of main-gear legs (each with its own wheel bogie), left+right combined. 0 = auto: 2 (one per side) below mlg_body_gear_mtow_kg, 4 (adds centreline body gear, e.g. A380/747-class) above it -- real widebodies above roughly 300 t add body gear because a two-leg bogie would need an impractically large tire count/track width to carry the load within tire-pressure limits.
fields.label: Main-gear strut count (0 = auto)
fields.name: n_mlg_struts

fields.help: Auto-sizing adds two centreline body-gear legs (4 main legs total) above this MTOW.
fields.label: MTOW threshold for body (centreline) main gear
fields.name: mlg_body_gear_mtow_kg

fields.help: 0 = auto: the smallest of {2, 4, 6} standard bogie sizes whose rated capacity (tire_safety_factor-derated) covers this strut's static reaction load at the aft CG limit.
fields.label: Wheels per main-gear strut (0 = auto)
fields.name: wheels_per_mlg_strut

fields.help: Main-gear lateral track width, as a multiple of fuselage diameter. Real transports with wing-root-mounted main gear run track/diameter ~1.75-2.0 (777-300ER 2.03, 787-9 1.90, A340-300 1.91, A380-800 2.00, A320-200 1.92, DC-10-30 1.77) -- 1.85 is the fleet-average calibration. An earlier default (1.15) understated real track width by roughly a factor of 1.6, which fed directly into the lateral-turnover check (physics.landing_gear) reading artificially safe.
fields.label: Main-gear track / fuselage-diameter factor
fields.name: track_diameter_factor

fields.help: Which reference tire (see physics.landing_gear.TIRE_DATABASE) to size with -- 'auto' picks the smallest class whose rated load, combined with a realistic wheel count (<=6/strut), covers the aircraft's static gear loads. Options: auto, light, narrowbody, widebody, heavy.
fields.label: Tire class
fields.name: tire_class

fields.help: Landing-gear strut/piston material, shown on the planform diagram and in the design report. 'auto' selects by MTOW class (see physics.landing_gear.STRUT_MATERIALS): high-strength steel (300M-class) for larger transports, an aluminium/steel combination for light aircraft. Informational/labelling only -- this preliminary-design tool does not run a structural (FEA) stress analysis of the strut itself.
fields.label: Strut material
fields.name: strut_material

fields.help: Lateral tip-over (overturn) criterion, Raymer Ch.11 / Currey convention: the angle from the vertical whose tangent is CG height over the CG's perpendicular distance to the nose-gear-to-main-gear ground line must not exceed this (evaluated at the forward CG limit, the worst case), or the aircraft risks tipping over in a tight turn. 63 deg is the standard transport-category limit; a higher CG, narrower track, or more forward CG all push the angle up toward it.
fields.label: Max lateral turnover angle
fields.name: turnover_angle_limit_deg

fields.help: Max time allowed for one mesh-generation (mset) call before it's killed.
fields.label: MSET timeout
fields.name: timeout_mset_s

fields.help: Max time allowed for one flow-solve (mses) call before it's killed.
fields.label: MSES timeout
fields.name: timeout_mses_s

fields.help: Newton iteration cap per angle of attack -- MSES reports non-convergence rather than looping forever, but a hard cap keeps a single stubborn point from stalling the whole sweep.
fields.label: Max solver iterations
fields.name: max_iterations

fields.help: e^N transition-prediction critical amplification factor. 9.0 is the standard sea-level-cruise default (Drela); lower values (e.g. 4-5) predict earlier transition, appropriate for a high-turbulence/rough-surface environment.
fields.label: Transition N-crit
fields.name: n_crit

fields.help: Force transition at this upper-surface x/c instead of letting MSES predict it. 1.0 = free (natural) transition, the realistic default for a clean cruise wing.
fields.label: Forced transition x/c, upper surface
fields.name: xtr_upper

fields.help: Force transition at this lower-surface x/c. 1.0 = free (natural) transition.
fields.label: Forced transition x/c, lower surface
fields.name: xtr_lower

fields.help: The MSES polar sweeps [trim_alpha - this, trim_alpha + this] so the comparison brackets the actual cruise operating point, not an arbitrary fixed range.
fields.label: Alpha sweep half-width around the trimmed design point
fields.name: alpha_sweep_halfwidth_deg

fields.help: Number of alpha points in the MSES polar sweep. Kept small relative to AeroSandbox's own VLM sweep (analysis.sweep_n_points) since each MSES point is a real viscous-compressible solve (~1-2s) rather than a linear-algebra VLM solve.
fields.label: Alpha sweep point count
fields.name: alpha_sweep_n_points

fields.help: Number of surface panel nodes MSET generates for the airfoil mesh.
fields.label: MSET panel count (n)
fields.name: mset_n

fields.help: Streamwise grid stretching parameter for the MSET mesh -- larger values cluster more points near the airfoil.
fields.label: MSET grid density exponent (e)
fields.name: mset_e

fields.help: Fraction of MTOW treated as 'suspended' mass in the Torenbeek wing structural formula (everything the wing structure must carry other than itself). Typical commercial transport: 0.70-0.78.
fields.label: Wing suspended-mass fraction
fields.name: suspended_mass_fraction

fields.help: Design airspeed with flaps extended, fed into the Torenbeek wing-mass formula.
fields.label: Max airspeed with flaps extended
fields.name: max_airspeed_for_flaps_ms

fields.help: Maximum flap deflection angle, fed into the Torenbeek wing-mass formula.
fields.label: Max take-off flap deflection
fields.name: flap_deflection_angle_deg

fields.help: Landing gear mass as a fraction of MTOW. Raymer Table 15.2: ~4% for commercial jet transports.
fields.label: Landing-gear mass fraction
fields.name: landing_gear_mass_fraction

fields.help: Dry engine mass is estimated as thrust / (this factor * g). Historical engine thrust-to-weight ratios are ~5-7, so this factor is typically ~6.
fields.label: Engine thrust-to-weight factor
fields.name: propulsion_twr_factor

fields.help: Multiplier on dry engine mass accounting for pylon, cowling, fire suppression and other installed accessories.
fields.label: Propulsion installation overhead
fields.name: propulsion_installation_factor

fields.help: Fallback propulsion mass as a fraction of MTOW, used only if the selected engine isn't found in the database.
fields.label: Propulsion mass fallback fraction
fields.name: propulsion_mass_fallback_fraction

fields.help: Avionics, electrical, ECS, APU, etc. as a fraction of MTOW. Raymer Table 15.2: 9-13% for commercial transports.
fields.label: Systems & equipment mass fraction
fields.name: systems_mass_fraction

fields.help: Passenger seats, galleys, lavatories, insulation, crew, paint, and operational empty items as a fraction of MTOW. Typically 10-14% for passenger transports.
fields.label: Furnishings & operations mass fraction
fields.name: furnishings_mass_fraction

fields.help: How much payload mass occupies one metre of cabin length. Used only to derive the payload/systems CG position (the occupied cabin length), not the payload mass itself -- so stretching the fuselage beyond what the payload needs doesn't shift the CG aft 'for free'.
fields.label: Payload linear density
fields.name: cabin_payload_density_kg_m

fields.help: Nose landing gear longitudinal position, as a fraction of total fuselage length from the nose.
fields.label: Nose-gear X position
fields.name: nlg_x_fraction

fields.help: Main landing gear longitudinal position, as a fraction of the mean aerodynamic chord aft of the MAC leading edge.
fields.label: Main-gear X position
fields.name: mlg_x_fraction_mac
fields.unit: fraction of MAC aft of MAC LE

fields.help: Maximum fraction of total aircraft weight the nose gear is rated to carry -- sets the 'NLG Max Strength' CG-envelope boundary.
fields.label: Max nose-gear load fraction
fields.name: pct_load_nlg_max

fields.help: Maximum fraction of total aircraft weight the main gear is rated to carry -- sets the 'MLG Max Strength' CG-envelope boundary.
fields.label: Max main-gear load fraction
fields.name: pct_load_mlg_max

fields.help: Minimum fraction of weight that must be on the nose gear for adequate steering authority -- sets the 'Min Nose Load' CG-envelope boundary (the aft-most safe CG at each weight).
fields.label: Min nose-gear load fraction
fields.name: pct_load_nlg_min

fields.help: Maximum Landing Weight (MLW) as a fraction of MTOW, shown as a reference line on the CG envelope.
fields.label: Max landing weight fraction of MTOW
fields.name: mlw_fraction_mtow

fields.help: Jet-A/Jet-A1 density at 15C (~804 kg/m^3). Converts wing tank volume to a fuel-mass capacity for the payload-range diagram and the wing fuel-volume check.
fields.label: Fuel density
fields.name: fuel_density_kg_m3

fields.help: Fraction of the wing's geometric (Torenbeek) fuel volume that's actually usable tank capacity, after structure, ribs, systems and unusable-fuel allowance. Typical preliminary-design value: 0.85-0.95.
fields.label: Usable fuel-tank volume fraction
fields.name: fuel_tank_usable_fraction

fields.help: When your most recent SimBrief OFP is for a different city pair than the departure/arrival airports selected above, fly the OFP's pair instead. A real dispatched OFP (real SID/STAR/airways, current AIRAC) is the most accurate route ALAS can get, so it takes precedence. Turn off to keep the manually-selected airports and ignore a mismatched OFP.
fields.label: SimBrief overrides route airports
fields.name: simbrief_overrides_airports

fields.help: Primary reward multiplier on L/D. Raise to prioritize aerodynamic efficiency over all penalties below.
fields.label: L/D reward weight
fields.name: ld_weight

fields.help: Penalizes cruise trim alpha outside [alpha_min_penalty_deg, alpha_max_penalty_deg]. Zero cost inside the window, quadratic outside. Kept small so the optimizer focuses on L/D.
fields.label: Trim-alpha penalty weight
fields.name: alpha_penalty_scale

fields.help: Lower bound of the acceptable cruise trim-alpha window (no penalty above this).
fields.label: Trim-alpha window: minimum
fields.name: alpha_min_penalty_deg

fields.help: Upper bound of the acceptable cruise trim-alpha window (no penalty below this).
fields.label: Trim-alpha window: maximum
fields.name: alpha_max_penalty_deg

fields.help: Small linear penalty per metre of span -- discourages excessively large wings.
fields.label: Wingspan penalty (per metre)
fields.name: span_penalty_per_m

fields.help: Rewards lower parasite drag (CD0); a thinner/cleaner shape reduces this term's cost. Typical cruise CD0 is 0.016-0.020.
fields.label: Parasite-drag (CD0) penalty weight
fields.name: cd0_penalty_scale

fields.help: Penalty per m^2 the wing area exceeds requirements.max_wing_area_m2.
fields.label: Max wing-area penalty weight
fields.name: area_penalty_scale

fields.help: Penalty per (kg/m^2)^2 below requirements.min_wing_loading_kg_m2.
fields.label: Min wing-loading penalty weight
fields.name: wing_loading_penalty_scale

fields.help: NOT read by the cost function (objective.py) -- kept only so old saved YAML configs referencing this key still load without error. Originally intended to penalize (Delta x_cg / MAC)^2, but that formula was never actually wired up; the field's real runtime effect was fully redundant with static_margin_penalty_scale, since both applied to the identical static-margin-vs-target term, so the two are consolidated into that single, correctly-named, appropriately-soft term. Physical CG-envelope compliance is enforced separately by cg_envelope_penalty_scale/cg_envelope_reward below.
fields.label: (Legacy, unused) CG/aero-balance mismatch weight
fields.name: cg_penalty_scale

fields.help: Penalizes the physical CG exceeding the [fwd, aft] CG envelope limits (% MAC, from Design Requirements). At 5% MAC beyond the limit the cost is comparable to one L/D unit, rising steeply further out.
fields.label: CG-envelope violation penalty weight
fields.name: cg_envelope_penalty_scale

fields.help: Reward applied to cost if the aircraft's entire operational CG envelope is within limits.
fields.label: CG-envelope compliance reward
fields.name: cg_envelope_reward

fields.help: Penalizes negative fuel mass (OEW + payload exceeding MTOW), normalized by MTOW.
fields.label: Negative-fuel penalty weight
fields.name: fuel_penalty_scale

fields.help: Penalizes the wing's physical usable fuel-tank volume (physics.performance.wing_fuel_volume_m3, Torenbeek geometric estimate) being too small to hold the fuel mass the weight & balance analysis says this design actually needs -- a wing that's too thin/small/tapered to carry its own required fuel is not a buildable aircraft, independent of whether the MTOW fuel-mass budget itself closes. Quadratic on the fractional shortfall (required_fuel - tank_capacity) / required_fuel.
fields.label: Insufficient wing fuel-volume penalty weight
fields.name: fuel_volume_penalty_scale

fields.help: SOFT preference nudging compliant-but-suboptimal candidates toward requirements.target_static_margin -- NOT a hard requirement (the physical floor, min_physical_static_margin, and the CG-envelope itself are enforced separately and are what actually keep a design safe/legal). Kept deliberately small relative to -L/D (typically 15-25) so this doesn't crowd out genuine aerodynamic improvements: raising it much above ~20-30 risks the optimizer chasing an exact SM match instead of exploring shape space, overwhelming the L/D signal the search is meant to prioritize.
fields.label: Static-margin target penalty weight
fields.name: static_margin_penalty_scale

fields.help: Minimum allowed airfoil thickness scale (relative to the reference section) before the thickness penalty kicks in.
fields.label: Minimum airfoil thickness scale
fields.name: thickness_floor

fields.help: Penalty weight applied when the morphed airfoil thickness collapses below thickness_floor.
fields.label: Thin-airfoil penalty weight
fields.name: thickness_penalty_scale

fields.help: Minimum allowed fuselage length before the too-short-fuselage penalty kicks in.
fields.label: Minimum fuselage length
fields.name: fuselage_floor_m

fields.help: Penalty weight applied when the fuselage shrinks below fuselage_floor_m.
fields.label: Too-short-fuselage penalty weight
fields.name: fuselage_penalty_scale

fields.help: Minimum allowed horizontal-stabiliser area as a fraction of wing area. Typical transports: ~20-30%. Prevents a 'tiny tail on a huge moment arm' cheat.
fields.label: Minimum H-stab area fraction
fields.name: min_hstab_area_fraction

fields.help: Minimum allowed vertical-stabiliser area as a fraction of wing area. Typical transports: ~8-14%.
fields.label: Minimum V-stab area fraction
fields.name: min_vstab_area_fraction

fields.help: Penalty weight for tail area fractions below their minimums (stiff quadratic).
fields.label: Tail-area-deficit penalty weight
fields.name: tail_area_penalty_scale

fields.help: Lower bound on the horizontal-tail volume coefficient Vh = Sh*Lh/(S*c_bar), which captures tail effectiveness accounting for its moment arm, not just area (Etkin/Reid convention).
fields.label: Minimum H-stab volume coefficient (Vh)
fields.name: min_hstab_volume_coef

fields.help: Upper bound on Vh -- penalises an oversized tail / an unnecessarily stretched fuselage moment arm.
fields.label: Maximum H-stab volume coefficient (Vh)
fields.name: max_hstab_volume_coef

fields.help: Lower bound on the vertical-tail volume coefficient Vv = Sv*Lv/(S*b).
fields.label: Minimum V-stab volume coefficient (Vv)
fields.name: min_vstab_volume_coef

fields.help: Upper bound on Vv (typical jet-transport max is ~0.12).
fields.label: Maximum V-stab volume coefficient (Vv)
fields.name: max_vstab_volume_coef

fields.help: Quadratic penalty weight for Vh/Vv falling outside their [min, max] bounds.
fields.label: Tail-volume-coefficient penalty weight
fields.name: tail_volume_penalty_scale

fields.help: Upper bound on break_chord_m / root_chord_m. Real transport wings taper noticeably from root to the yehudi break (typically 0.45-0.65); without this bound the optimizer can inflate the break chord toward the root chord to enlarge MAC (c_ref) 'for free', which cheapens every %MAC-normalised penalty (CG envelope, static-margin target) without a real stability improvement. Soft penalty above this ratio, not a hard bound.
fields.label: Max break/root chord ratio
fields.name: max_break_root_chord_ratio

fields.help: Penalty weight applied when break_chord_m / root_chord_m exceeds max_break_root_chord_ratio.
fields.label: Break-chord taper-realism penalty weight
fields.name: taper_realism_penalty_scale

fields.help: Penalizes the wing's root-to-break trailing edge (seen in planform) making an angle greater than 90 deg with the fuselage centerline -- i.e. the break station's trailing edge sitting forward of the root's. That creates a reflex (concave) corner at the wing-fuselage junction: a severe stress concentration no real transport-category wing root has, caused by a short root chord combined with a comparatively long break chord and/or too little sweep. Quadratic on the angle exceedance beyond 90 deg.
fields.label: Wing-root trailing-edge angle penalty weight
fields.name: te_root_angle_penalty_scale

fields.help: Wing-root leading edge must sit at least this fraction of fuselage length aft of the nose -- prevents the optimizer placing the wing in the cockpit. Typical transports: 25-55%.
fields.label: Minimum wing position (fraction of fuselage length)
fields.name: min_wing_position_fraction

fields.help: Penalty weight applied when the wing sits forward of min_wing_position_fraction.
fields.label: Wing-too-far-forward penalty weight
fields.name: wing_position_penalty_scale

fields.help: Steep quadratic penalty on the fractional shortfall vs. the target passenger count / cargo payload -- guides the optimizer to grow the fuselage long enough to actually fit the requested payload.
fields.label: Payload-shortfall penalty weight
fields.name: payload_shortfall_penalty_scale

fields.help: Maximum allowed fuselage length/diameter ratio before the too-slender-fuselage penalty kicks in.
fields.label: Maximum fuselage fineness ratio
fields.name: fineness_ratio_max

fields.help: Penalty weight applied when the fuselage fineness ratio exceeds fineness_ratio_max.
fields.label: Slender-fuselage penalty weight
fields.name: fineness_ratio_penalty_scale

fields.help: Cost returned for any candidate design that raises an exception or fails a hard guard during evaluation.
fields.label: Invalid-design cost
fields.name: failure_cost

fields.help: Severity scale for the static-margin-floor penalty applied to a candidate that builds and analyses successfully but is rejected as physically invalid (static margin below requirements.min_physical_static_margin). NOT a flat returned cost -- this floor is graduated, not an early return (objective.py's `(deficit * severity)**3` term, where this field sets `severity` so raising/lowering it steepens/relaxes the penalty without editing code; the default reproduces the exact cubic constant used before this field was wired up). Kept distinct from failure_cost so run diagnostics can tell 'geometry/analysis crashed' apart from 'physically unstable' rejects (see OptimizationHistory.reject_reason_counts).
fields.label: Instability reject cost
fields.name: instability_failure_cost

fields.help: SciPy differential_evolution strategy name (e.g. 'best1bin', 'rand1bin', 'best2bin') -- controls how new candidate designs are generated from the population each generation.
fields.label: DE mutation/crossover strategy
fields.name: strategy

fields.help: Maximum number of generations (iterations) the solver runs before stopping.
fields.label: Max generations
fields.name: max_iterations

fields.help: Population size as a multiplier on the number of design variables -- more candidates per generation explores more broadly but costs more evaluations.
fields.label: Population size multiplier
fields.name: population_size

fields.help: Relative tolerance for convergence; the solver stops early once the population's cost spread falls below this.
fields.label: Convergence tolerance
fields.name: tolerance

fields.help: Set an integer for a reproducible run (same seed -> same result); leave blank for a different search each run.
fields.label: Random seed
fields.name: seed

fields.help: Number of worker processes for parallel evaluation (>1 uses multiprocessing). Requires a picklable objective -- already the case for ALAS's optimizer.
fields.label: Parallel worker processes
fields.name: workers

fields.help: Print a one-line progress summary (valid count, best L/D so far) after each generation.
fields.label: Print progress to console
fields.name: display_progress

fields.help: Initialize the population as a tight cluster of small perturbations around the initial/preset design (plus the design itself, unperturbed) instead of SciPy's default uniform latin-hypercube coverage of the whole bounds space. Guarantees at least one known-valid, physically-balanced design is in generation 0, and lets the solver refine from there instead of having to rediscover CG/stability balance from scratch across the full 16-D space. Disable to fall back to the old full-space exploration (e.g. if you specifically want to explore far from the initial design).
fields.label: Seed search near the initial design
fields.name: seed_near_initial_design

fields.help: Size of the initial random perturbation around the initial design, as a fraction of each design variable's (upper - lower) bound range. Only used when seed_near_initial_design is enabled. Small values (e.g. 0.05) start with a tight, mostly-valid cluster; larger values explore more broadly from the start at the cost of more of the population starting off invalid.
fields.label: Seed cluster perturbation size
fields.name: seed_perturbation_fraction

fields.help: Maximum lift coefficient achievable in the take-off flap/slat configuration. Drives take-off field length via the matching chart.
fields.label: Max lift coefficient, take-off (CLmax_TO)
fields.name: cl_max_to

fields.help: Maximum lift coefficient achievable in the landing flap/slat configuration. Drives landing distance.
fields.label: Max lift coefficient, landing (CLmax_L)
fields.name: cl_max_land

fields.help: Maximum lift coefficient in clean (flaps/slats up) configuration -- the true aerodynamic stall limit used for the V-n diagram's stall boundary, distinct from the flaps-down CLmax_TO/CLmax_L above.
fields.label: Max lift coefficient, clean (CLmax_clean)
fields.name: cl_max_clean

fields.help: Most negative (inverted-flight) lift coefficient in clean configuration -- the negative stall boundary on the V-n diagram.
fields.label: Min lift coefficient, clean (CLmin_clean)
fields.name: cl_min_clean

fields.help: Fraction by which static sea-level thrust falls off during the take-off ground roll / initial climb, used in the matching-chart take-off constraint.
fields.label: Thrust lapse ratio
fields.name: thrust_lapse

fields.help: FAR 25.121 minimum second-segment climb gradient with one engine inoperative (OEI). The matching chart auto-selects 0.024 (twin) / 0.027 (tri-jet) / 0.030 (quad) from the actual engine count; this value is only the fallback for any other engine count.
fields.label: OEI 2nd-segment climb gradient (fallback)
fields.name: oei_gradient

fields.help: Empirical constant relating approach speed / wing loading to landing ground-roll + air distance.
fields.label: Landing distance factor (k_land)
fields.name: k_land

fields.help: Lift coefficient assumed in the take-off configuration when evaluating OEI second-segment climb L/D (Raymer Ch.17).
fields.label: OEI climb configuration CL
fields.name: oei_climb_cl

fields.help: Parasite-drag increment added to the clean CD0 for the flap/gear-down OEI second-segment climb configuration.
fields.label: OEI climb flap/gear drag increment
fields.name: oei_climb_delta_cd

fields.help: Lower wing-loading (W/S) axis limit on the matching chart plot. Widen for very light (GA) aircraft. (~204 kg/m^2)
fields.label: Matching chart wing-loading axis: minimum
fields.name: ws_min_pa

fields.help: Upper wing-loading (W/S) axis limit on the matching chart plot. Widen for very heavy (freighter) aircraft. (~1020 kg/m^2)
fields.label: Matching chart wing-loading axis: maximum
fields.name: ws_max_pa

fields.help: BFL = bfl_factor x TODR (take-off distance required). Raymer Table 17.1: 1.15 for twin jets, ~1.18 for quads.
fields.label: Balanced field length factor
fields.name: bfl_factor

fields.help: Minimum-control speed as a multiple of take-off stall speed. FAR 25.149 caps VMC at 1.13*VSR; that ceiling is used as the default.
fields.label: VMC / VS_TO
fields.name: vmc_vstall_factor

fields.help: FAR 25.107: rotation speed must be at least 1.05*VMC.
fields.label: VR / VMC floor
fields.name: vr_vmc_factor

fields.help: FAR 25.107: rotation speed must also be at least 1.10*VS_TO. VR = max(vr_vmc_factor*VMC, vr_vstall_factor*VS_TO).
fields.label: VR / VS_TO floor
fields.name: vr_vstall_factor

fields.help: Take-off safety speed as a multiple of take-off stall speed (FAR 25.107). V2 = max(v2_vstall_factor*VS_TO, VR).
fields.label: V2 / VS_TO
fields.name: v2_vstall_factor

fields.help: Decision speed as a fraction of rotation speed. On a dry balanced field V1 sits just below VR (~0.95-0.98); the earlier 0.90 default put V1 unrealistically far below VR (e.g. ~152 kt against a real 787-9 V1 of 160-165 kt).
fields.label: V1 / VR
fields.name: v1_vr_factor

fields.help: Approach speed as a multiple of landing stall speed (FAR 25.125).
fields.label: VAPP / VS_land
fields.name: vapp_vstall_land_factor

fields.help: Touchdown speed as a multiple of landing stall speed.
fields.label: VTD / VS_land
fields.name: vtd_vstall_land_factor

fields.help: Number of wing-loading points swept when drawing the matching-chart constraint curves (Results -> Matching Chart). Purely a plotting resolution knob -- higher gives smoother curves at extra compute cost. Not part of the Performance preset (it isn't a physical assumption).
fields.label: Matching chart plot resolution
fields.name: matching_chart_resolution

fields.help: Total-pressure recovery through the inlet (ram + duct losses). Matches SUAVE's inlet_nozzle.pressure_ratio.
fields.label: Inlet pressure recovery
fields.name: inlet_pressure_recovery

fields.help: Fixed low-pressure-compressor (booster) pressure ratio; the high-pressure compressor makes up the rest of the overall (core) pressure ratio (HPC = OPR / this value). Matches SUAVE's fixed LPC split.
fields.label: LPC pressure-ratio split
fields.name: lpc_pressure_ratio_split

fields.help: Total-pressure loss fraction across the combustor.
fields.label: Combustor pressure ratio
fields.name: combustor_pressure_ratio

fields.help: Shaft power-transmission efficiency for both spools (HPT-HPC, LPT-LPC+fan).
fields.label: Turbine mechanical efficiency
fields.name: turbine_mechanical_efficiency

fields.help: Polytropic expansion efficiency of the core exhaust nozzle.
fields.label: Core nozzle efficiency
fields.name: core_nozzle_efficiency

fields.help: Polytropic expansion efficiency of the fan (bypass) nozzle.
fields.label: Fan nozzle efficiency
fields.name: fan_nozzle_efficiency

fields.help: Lower heating value of Jet-A/Jet-A1 fuel.
fields.label: Fuel heating value
fields.name: fuel_heating_value_kj_kg

fields.help: Air-standard specific heat used for the inlet/fan/compressor (unburned-air) stations.
fields.label: Cold-section specific heat (cp)
fields.name: cp_cold_j_kgk

fields.help: Combustion-gas specific heat used for the combustor/turbine/core-nozzle stations.
fields.label: Hot-section specific heat (cp)
fields.name: cp_hot_j_kgk

fields.help: Used only to sanity-check the design mass flow implied by anchoring the cycle to the engine's rated static thrust -- a conceptual-design-level assumption, not a real corrected-flow schedule.
fields.label: Assumed fan-face Mach number (static anchor)
fields.name: fan_face_mach

fields.help: Size a generic wingbox (skin/spars/ribs) for the optimized design's main wing, write NASTRAN .bdf files, and compute theoretical (no-NASTRAN) deformations/stresses/frequencies as part of a normal Run, populating the Structural Analysis Results tab. Does not affect the mass model, CG, or optimizer -- purely a downstream analysis, like MSES/Propulsion Analysis.
fields.label: Enabled
fields.name: enabled

fields.help: Chordwise position of each spar, as a fraction of local chord (0=leading edge, 1=trailing edge). One entry per spar, any order (sorted automatically). E.g. (0.25, 0.70) is a classic front/rear 2-spar box; add a third entry for a mid-spar.
fields.label: Spar chord positions
fields.name: spar_chord_fractions

fields.help: Which ribs get trailing-edge panels (rear-spar to TE), preventing TE buckling: 'all', 'none', 'alternate', 'inboard' (only inboard of the wing break), 'outboard', or 'step_N' (every Nth rib).
fields.label: Trailing-edge rib panel mode
fields.name: te_rib_mode

fields.help: Adds an optional third spar running only from the root to the wing break/kink station, at center_spar_chord_fraction of local chord -- the partial-span reinforcement spar common on widebody wings (extra bending/shear capacity where root load is highest, without the mass of running it all the way to the tip). Off by default (classic 2-spar box). This spar carries no load and contributes no mass outboard of the kink -- it simply doesn't exist there.
fields.label: Add center spar (root-to-kink)
fields.name: center_spar_enabled

fields.help: Chordwise position of the optional center spar (see center_spar_enabled), as a fraction of local chord. Only used when center_spar_enabled is True.
fields.label: Center spar chord position
fields.name: center_spar_chord_fraction

fields.help: Material name from the built-in structural material database, used for the wing skin panels.
fields.label: Skin material
fields.name: skin_material

fields.help: Material for the spar shear webs.
fields.label: Spar web material
fields.name: spar_web_material

fields.help: Material for the spar caps (the primary bending-load-carrying members).
fields.label: Spar cap material
fields.name: spar_cap_material

fields.help: Material for the rib webs.
fields.label: Rib material
fields.name: rib_material

fields.help: Extra margin multiplied onto the design loads on top of the CS-25 ultimate load factors already used (DesignRequirements.ultimate_load_factor / limit_load_factor_neg). 1.0 = no extra margin beyond CS-25 ultimate.
fields.label: Additional safety factor
fields.name: additional_safety_factor

fields.help: Wing skin thickness -- this is the value actually used (no shear-flow/buckling upsizing is modeled, see structural_sizing.py), so treat it as a practical starting assumption for this class of aircraft, not a bare absolute-minimum gauge. 6mm matches the reference sizing scripts' own baseline for a large long-range wing; a much thinner value (e.g. 2mm) understates real skin panel buckling resistance and inflates the auto-derived rib count substantially, since rib spacing scales with sqrt(t_skin).
fields.label: Skin gauge
fields.name: t_skin_min_m

fields.help: Spanwise fraction below which spar caps keep their full root section (bending moment is highest inboard, so locking the section here preserves most of the tip-deflection stiffness). Above this station, caps taper linearly down to cap_taper_tip_fraction at the tip.
fields.label: Cap taper lock station
fields.name: cap_taper_eta_lock

fields.help: Fraction of the locked-section cap flange width/thickness remaining at the wingtip.
fields.label: Cap taper tip fraction
fields.name: cap_taper_tip_fraction

fields.help: Empirical panel-buckling coefficient (c) in the Euler skin-panel critical stress formula used to auto-derive rib spacing/count -- higher allows wider rib spacing for the same skin thickness.
fields.label: Rib spacing buckling coefficient
fields.name: rib_buckling_coeff

fields.help: Effective radius of gyration of a skin panel stiffened by a stringer, used by the same rib-spacing buckling formula.
fields.label: Stiffened-panel radius of gyration
fields.name: rib_radius_of_gyration_m

fields.help: Force an exact number of ribs instead of the auto-derived panel-buckling spacing. Leave blank to let the app determine rib count/spacing.
fields.label: Rib count override
fields.name: num_ribs_override

fields.help: Number of spanwise points used for load/moment/deflection integration (sizing and the analytical deformation/stress solver). Higher = smoother curves, slower.
fields.label: Spanwise integration stations
fields.name: spanwise_stations

fields.help: Number of chordwise points sampled per rib cross-section in the FEM mesh.
fields.label: Mesh chordwise points per rib
fields.name: mesh_chordwise_points

fields.help: Pull-up / push-down / 1g-level static load cases -> deformation and stress.
fields.label: Run static analysis (SOL 101)
fields.name: run_sol_static

fields.help: Natural frequencies and mode shapes.
fields.label: Run normal modes (SOL 103)
fields.name: run_sol_modes

fields.help: Modal frequency response to a harmonic engine-mounted excitation force.
fields.label: Run sine sweep (SOL 111)
fields.name: run_sol_vibration_sine

fields.help: Modal random-vibration response (PSD) to a white-noise engine-mounted excitation.
fields.label: Run random vibration (SOL 111)
fields.name: run_sol_vibration_random

fields.help: Max time allowed for one NASTRAN solution (SOL 101/103/111 each run separately) before it's killed.
fields.label: NASTRAN timeout per solution
fields.name: timeout_s

fields.help: Max structural modes for SOL 103's EIGRL and the analytical Rayleigh-quotient estimate.
fields.label: Number of modes to extract
fields.name: n_modes

fields.help: Structural damping assumed for the sine/random vibration response (2% is a common metallic-airframe assumption).
fields.label: Modal damping ratio
fields.name: modal_damping_ratio

fields.help: Flat white-noise acceleration power spectral density applied at the excitation point for the random-vibration case.
fields.label: Random vibration base PSD
fields.name: psd_base_g2_per_hz
